title: Finite purity conjugates actual exceptional tower reduction
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a smooth separated morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$, and put $R_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n=A_{E,en}$ for $n\geq1$. Use the ordinary derived categories of strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], their uniform constructible finite-Tor full subcategories $\mathcal C_T=\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], and ordinary derived tensor products [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Twists are [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and $F_\bullet=Rf_{!,\bullet}\dashv G_\bullet=f^!_\bullet$ with finite units, counits and evaluations is [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Put $\mathbf1_{\bullet,T}=(R_{n,T})_n$ and $\omega_\bullet=G_\bullet\mathbf1_{\bullet,Y}$, so $\omega_n=f^!_{R_n}R_{n,Y}$; pullback means levelwise finite derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Let $K_\bullet\in\mathcal C_Y$ with canonical reductions $\rho^K_{n,m}:(K_n)_{R_m}\to K_m$ [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], and put $P_\bullet=f_\bullet^*K_\bullet(d)[2d]$. This tower belongs to $\mathcal C_X$; if the $K_n$ have common Tor interval $[a,b]$, its common cohomological and Tor interval is $[a-2d,b-2d]$. Under the canonical derived pullback, twist and coefficient identifications [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso, det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], its actual reductions are
$$\rho^P_{n,m}=f^*_{R_m}(\rho^K_{n,m})(d)[2d].$$
Let $c_{n,m}$ be the exceptional coefficient comparison [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities], and let $\gamma_{f,R_n}$ be the finite inverse-diagonal-orientation/tensor-transpose map [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], identified with the general-ring purity map [det-sp-finite-general-ring]. The actual reductions of $G_\bullet K_\bullet$ and their purity square satisfy
$$\rho^{GK}_{n,m}=f^!_{R_m}(\rho^K_{n,m})\circ c_{n,m}(K_n),$$
$$\rho^{GK}_{n,m}\circ(\gamma_{f,R_n}(K_n))_{R_m}=\gamma_{f,R_m}(K_m)\circ\rho^P_{n,m}.$$
In particular, since the finite purity comparisons are isomorphisms,
$$\rho^{GK}_{n,m}=\gamma_{f,R_m}(K_m)\circ\rho^P_{n,m}\circ((\gamma_{f,R_n}(K_n))_{R_m})^{-1}.$$
These formulas hold without a normalization assumption on $K_\bullet$, for nonflat quotient coefficient maps as well, and use scalar extension with its target-ring module structure.

proof.text: Apply lem-sp-purity-pullback-level-bounds separately at each positive coefficient level to obtain constructibility and the shifted Tor interval. Test the intrinsic Tor interval against the coefficient unit: transport to the fixed-ring derived presentation by intrinsic_hasProEtaleTorAmplitude_iff_torAmplitudeIn, apply homologyConcentratedIn_of_torAmplitudeIn, and transport cohomology back through the exact realization. Unpack the input tower common Tor interval [c,t], apply the single-level result at every n, and use [c-2d,t-2d] for both uniform output intervals in sk-def-sp-normalized-towers. The two interval inequalities follow by subtracting the same 2d. Separately repeat the level calculation for any specified common input interval [a,z] to obtain the quantified bounds. This is the complete Lean proof of pullbackTower_bounds; its only new open step is the strictly single-level constructibility/Tor calculation.

proof.text: The comparisons are the unchanged definitions now owned by def-sp-purity-reduction-comparisons. Prove sourceComparison invertible: inputWord is a composite of isomorphisms; pullWord preserves this; the ordered line comparison is invertible by induction on d, using the unit at zero and tensor/root comparisons at successors. targetComparison is likewise a composite of isomorphisms. finiteGeneralRingOrientation supplies normalized alpha_n for every level. smooth_tensor_duality makes its ordinary gamma invertible at each origin. Define gamma_n as the inverse sourceComparison followed by the transported finite gamma and targetComparison. The normalization equation follows by hom-inverse cancellation.

proof.text: For m≤n apply pullback_reduction_transport to obtain the canonical line comparison e, actual origin arrow r, its origin equation hr and source reduction equation hp. Apply finite_purity_reduction_transport with the normalized orientations, e and r. Precompose the desired gamma square by scalar extension of sourceComparison(n), an isomorphism. Functor.map_comp and the normalization equation identify its left side with the finite beta square; hp and the normalization equation at m identify its right side. Cancellation proves the square. The first exceptional formula is exactly lv.reduction.
